\NLFrontMatterSection{Executive summary}

This specification decomposes every one of the 357 NL-TPS high-level interface requirements (HLIRs) into three implementation-facing obligations. Contract HLIRs become a controlled boundary definition, an executable schema and semantic profile, and an activation and change record. Runtime HLIRs become an ingress validation and safety gate, a deterministic transaction and outcome controller, and an observable reconciliation and recovery path. Evidence HLIRs become an objective verification protocol, retained integrated and commissioning results, and a release and lifecycle control. The resulting 1071 sub-interface requirements define the minimum work needed to bring each HLIR into being without selecting a vendor, deployment topology, or clinical threshold prematurely.

The NL-TPS remains a human-supervised team-of-teams environment. Existing commissioned TPS, PACS, OIS, imaging, dose, QA, and delivery systems remain authoritative within their approved roles. Generative or inference models may create bounded drafts and decision support but receive no independent authority to approve, export, or authorize treatment. DICOM and DICOM-RT remain the minimum portable external exchange foundation; optional vendor APIs, IHE-RO profiles, FHIR, or CodeX exchanges are bounded supplements that require their own controlled contracts and cannot bypass DICOM reconciliation, human approval, physics review, independent QA, or site commissioning.

\section{1. Purpose, scope, and derivation}
The controlled interface trace path addressed by this specification is:
\begin{center}
\textbf{ConOps} $\rightarrow$ \textbf{119 HLRs} $\rightarrow$ \textbf{357 HLIRs} $\rightarrow$ \textbf{1071 sub-interface requirements} $\rightarrow$ \textbf{61 interface components and 15 teams} $\rightarrow$ \textbf{verified routes and released capability}
\end{center}
The 357 detailed sub-requirements and their component allocations form a parallel branch beneath the HLR baseline. A capability is complete only when its functional behavior, interface behavior, components, people, procedures, evidence, and operational controls are integrated and accepted together. This document refines interface obligations only; it does not replace clinical procedures, hazard analysis, component specifications, DICOM conformance statements, verification protocols, commissioning reports, model cards, cybersecurity plans, or site-specific release records.

\section{2. Requirement identifiers and decomposition rules}
Sub-interface identifiers use \texttt{SIR-DOM-NNN-HH-SS}. \texttt{DOM-NNN} identifies the HLR ancestor, \texttt{HH} identifies its \texttt{IF-} child, and \texttt{SS} identifies one of three sub-interface children. For example, \texttt{SIR-PLN-004-02-03} is the third sub-interface child of \texttt{IF-PLN-004-02}. The words \textit{shall}, \textit{should}, and \textit{may} mean mandatory, recommended, and permitted.

Each HLIR is satisfied only when all three SIR children, every assigned interface-family subprofile, and all applicable release evidence are complete together. A child may not be treated as optional because a route is internal, uses a vendor API, or has passed a previous site test. Any tailoring requires approved trace, risk, architecture, clinical, quality, cybersecurity, and V\&V rationale.

\section{3. Sub-interface realization architecture}
Every deployed route shall have one controlled chain: authorized producer or user $\rightarrow$ ingress validation and safety decision $\rightarrow$ transaction or human interaction $\rightarrow$ authoritative consumer or system of record $\rightarrow$ explicit acknowledgment $\rightarrow$ reconciliation and retained evidence. The chain shall preserve patient and case identity, professional authority, object and configuration version, lifecycle state, provenance, security context, and failure status end to end.

A route may be synchronous, asynchronous, file- or object-based, event-driven, DICOM DIMSE, DICOMweb, IHE-profiled, vendor-API based, or human-mediated. The transport does not alter the safety obligation. Storage or transport success is not equivalent to semantic import, clinical acceptance, plan approval, QA completion, transfer authorization, or treatment-delivery authorization; those states require separate authoritative acknowledgments and reconciliation.

The standards baseline includes \href{https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part02/sect_n.3.3.html}{DICOM PS3.2 Conformance}, \href{https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part04/sect_6.7.html}{DICOM PS3.4 Service Class Specifications}, \href{https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part07/chapter_1.html}{DICOM PS3.7 Message Exchange}, \href{https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part15/PS3.15.html}{DICOM PS3.15 Security and System Management Profiles}, applicable radiotherapy information-object definitions in DICOM PS3.3, and the \href{https://profiles.ihe.net/RO/index.html}{IHE Radiation Oncology Technical Framework, Revision 4.0}. DICOM conformance is a necessary input to integration but does not replace validation with the specific equipment and workflow; the RP-VVP and RP-RLS requirements therefore make paired analysis, negative testing, semantic round-trip, site commissioning, and change regression mandatory.

\section{6. Team-of-teams delivery and approval}
The parent owner remains accountable for the HLIR outcome. Family leads own the accuracy of their subprofiles and implementation contributions. T-SYS controls cross-family architecture and safety state; T-DATA controls shared semantics, identity, provenance, and audit; T-SEC controls trust and privacy; T-OPS controls operability and recovery; T-VV maintains independent evidence; T-GOV controls release and change; and T-CLIN, T-PLAN, T-IMG, T-REV, medical physics, dosimetry, and other authorized specialists approve the clinical portions applicable to the route.

\addlinespace[2pt]

It shall reconcile producer, consumer, and system-of-record state; quarantine orphaned or partial outputs; alert the accountable team; and support safe retry, compensation, rollback, recovery, and incident linkage without bypassing a hard stop. & RP-OBS & T-NLI; T\slash\allowbreak{}A \\
\addlinespace[2pt]

An incompatible version, unresolved safety-significant failure, or uncommissioned route shall prevent clinical release. \textit{Assigned families: IF-NLI-01; IF-UI-01; IF-SAF-01; IF-EVD-01; IF-CTX-01; parent owner: T-NLI.}} \\

\section{8. External TPS, DICOM, and IHE-RO realization minimum}
Every route assigned IF-DICOM-01 or IF-TPS-01 shall produce one site- and version-specific RP-ICD, RP-SCH, RP-VAL, RP-TRX, RP-OBS, RP-VVP, and RP-RLS chain as applicable. The chain shall include:
\begin{itemize}
\item a real-world activity and data-flow description identifying each application entity or endpoint, initiator and responder, SCU and SCP or user-agent and origin-server roles, network and security parameters, association or HTTP behavior, and accountable organizations;
\item an allowlist of SOP Classes, transfer syntaxes, DIMSE services, DICOMweb resources, IHE-RO profiles and options where used, media profiles where used, and bounded vendor-API operations, with unsupported, private, specialized, extended, coerced, or lossy behavior explicitly identified;
\item object profiles for applicable images, registrations, segmentations or structure sets, RT Plan, RT Ion Plan, RT Dose, treatment records, and second-generation radiotherapy objects, including required and conditional attributes, terminology, units, geometry, and approval-state semantics;
\item patient, course, study, series, SOP Instance, Frame of Reference, plan, structure, dose, registration, machine, and delivery references; UID creation and preservation; reference-graph integrity; coordinate transforms; dose basis; and source-to-destination semantic fidelity;
\item association or session negotiation, capability discovery, authentication, authorization, encryption, timeout, retry, duplicate, idempotency, partial transfer, cancellation, rejection, status-code interpretation, quarantine, rollback, and downtime behavior;
\item separate transport, storage, semantic-import, clinical-review, approval, independent-QA, transfer-readiness, and destination-acceptance states so that a successful C-STORE or HTTP response is never treated as clinical acceptance or treatment authorization;
\item paired conformance statements and gap analysis, valid and invalid object examples, reference and geometry checks, private-attribute analysis, semantic round-trip comparison, import and export reconciliation, representative workflow tests, failure injection, and retained destination evidence;
\item for an optional vendor API, exact authentication, authorization, schema, version, supported operation, rate and timeout, error, audit, monitoring, change-notification, fallback, and authority limits, with reconciliation to the commissioned DICOM and TPS state; and
\item site acceptance and commissioning by vendor, product version, institution, machine, modality, technique, disease site, workflow, and configuration, plus known limitations, support, incident coordination, change triggers, regression scope, rollback, and release approval.
\end{itemize}
An IHE-RO profile may reduce local ambiguity by specifying actors, transactions, and content modules, but its use shall be versioned, option-specific, tested with the deployed actors, and reconciled with the authoritative DICOM objects and workflow states. Participation in a Connectathon or possession of an integration statement is useful evidence but does not replace site commissioning and clinical-workflow validation.

\section{9. Sub-interface definition of done}
A sub-interface requirement is complete only when all applicable conditions below are satisfied:
\begin{itemize}
\item the SIR traces without ambiguity to one HLIR, one HLR ancestor, assigned interface families, realization packages, components, hazards and risk controls, owners, test cases, results, anomalies, monitoring, and release records;
\item every deployed producer-consumer route has an approved RP-ICD and machine-validatable RP-SCH with controlled valid, invalid, boundary, and version examples;
\item RP-VAL, RP-TRX, and RP-OBS implement authorized normal, negative, duplicate, stale, wrong-context, timeout, retry, cancellation, partial, degraded, rollback, recovery, and reconciliation paths without silent substitution or authority expansion;
\item security, privacy, performance, capacity, availability, time synchronization, audit, provenance, retention, monitoring, incident, supplier, support, downtime, and recovery responsibilities are implemented and tested;
\item RP-VVP contains independent producer, consumer, integrated, human-factors where applicable, interoperability, failure-injection, commissioning, and acceptance evidence with all anomalies resolved or formally dispositioned;
\item RP-RLS binds the accepted route and compatibility matrix to approved versions, limitations, residual risks, training, monitoring thresholds, change and revalidation triggers, rollback, retirement, and accountable release authority; and
\item the complete team-of-teams review confirms that human professional authority, medical-physics and dosimetry responsibilities, independent QA, and commissioned-system controls remain intact.
\end{itemize}

\section{11. Controlled open sub-interface decisions}
The following decisions remain deployment-specific and shall be resolved through controlled architecture, clinical governance, interface control, vendor coordination, cybersecurity, operations, verification, commissioning, and change control before an affected route is activated:
\begin{itemize}
\item exact components, producers, consumers, users, endpoints, application entities, services, events, queues, files, schemas, content profiles, hosting, topology, network zones, and systems of record;
\item vendor, product and version, DICOM SOP Classes and roles, transfer syntaxes, DIMSE and DICOMweb services, IHE-RO profiles and options, private attributes, vendor APIs, and unsupported or lossy semantics;
\item disease-site, modality, technique, machine, prescription, contour, registration, dose, robustness, approval, and workflow semantics that require local profiles or cannot be transported portably;
\item terminology, nomenclature, identifiers, UID policy, units, coordinate transforms, rounding, precision, reference graphs, state mappings, authority mappings, conflict resolution, and authoritative-source precedence;
\item identity federation, credential and certificate lifecycle, service identity, secrets, encryption, audit transport, egress, minimum-necessary data, residency, retention, privacy, and incident coordination;
\item latency, throughput, capacity, availability, time synchronization, timeout, retry, idempotency, ordering, cancellation, compensation, downtime, recovery, and reconciliation limits and acceptance thresholds; and
\item final ownership, supplier responsibility, support model, change notification, compatibility and migration policy, monitoring thresholds, anomaly escalation, revalidation triggers, acceptance criteria, residual-risk authority, rollback, retirement, and release evidence.
\end{itemize}
\textbf{Bottom line. }A high-level interface requirement is brought into being only when its three SIR children, assigned family subprofiles, realization packages, implementations, people and procedures, evidence, and release controls are complete and operating together across the actual producer-consumer route.
